chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.title: Ordo Ab Chao
paras: Before it all began, Elzaiya had a predominant thought: perhaps the best way to control chaos was to create it.
Chaos, after all, was a reliable constant. Unlike order, which didn't benefit from disruption, chaos thrived in its unpredictability, which was the nature of the world's reality.

Chaos obeyed no laws, yet always behaved as its nature meant it to: erratic, untamed, but reliably consistent in its randomness. To control chaos, one needed not intelligence but instinct. Intelligence was linear, bound by logic and confined to patterns. Instinct, however, was something even the dullest animal had, which they've used to thrive through time, as evolution had taught. Instinct was primal, raw, and fluid enough to swim through chaos without drowning in it. Only those who had superior instincts had survived. Others, as intelligent as they'd been, were now extinct.
It was not the rational mind but instinct, the seat of intuition, that could anticipate the vibrations and dissonances of chaos.
He'd watched the spider and had learnt to understand the paradox of its web. Small enough to catch what needed to be caught, but big enough to allow the strongest winds to pass through.

The path through chaos wasn’t that of resistance or fear but immersion. By giving in to its swirling tides, anyone could ride the currents rather than drown. Mastery in this sea wasn’t about taming it but about understanding that in its formlessness and its formations, there was power. It meant embracing the truth: that nothing was stable, and that, that right there, was the highest form of life's stability.

On the afternoon of January 6th, supported by another anonymous witness who had claimed that they would come out of hiding ten months later to testify, Elzaiya was taken into witness protection and was later transferred to an undisclosed location in the United States, where he was to stay until he and the other witness had given their testimony in the case against Emerson for crimes committed, including multiple counts of murder, corporate espionage, fraud, and other illegal activities filed against him.

The case was reported in all the papers, headlined across all TV news channels, and hashtagged all over the internet. It was not the case against Emerson itself that caused the stir, but the fact that Elzaiya had named several of his co-perpetrators in his briefing before he was put into witness protection, two of whom were Harlequin and Aaira Quinn.

Elzaiya had confirmed, during the press briefing, that these two people, the most beloved of all the masses' political figures, had not merely been swept into but had been active players in Emerson's schemes to eliminate his late brother, Sarki, almost assassinate him, Elzaiya, for standing up to them, and eventually succeed in taking the life of the people's beloved Arden Quinn: their very own Aladdin. Elzaiya went so far as to reveal that the murder was committed by none other than his father's most beloved wife, Aaira, whom Quinn outed for having an affair with Emerson.
Like all sensational news, the media painted it red, added some strawberry to it, and made it smell like Christmas. And the public devoured it.
"You didn't have to go that far," Machiavelli said, muting the TV.
"Yeah, Elz, think what the people might later start to think. That you're just a heartless son who despises his mother," Cairo said.
When did I become Elz? Elzaiya thought.

“You're losing focus on the main picture,” Alpheus said. He slumped into the chair behind him and rubbed his palms on his knees. He's been overworked this week, being the one who had to make negotiations with his connections in the force to agree to go along with Elzaiya's plan of pretending to safeguard a fake witness.

Sure, witness protection and all had been set up, but Elzaiya had insisted they find someone else to pretend to be him. At the end of the day, he'd found a man who was his size and build and was willing to participate in their schemes for a price. Now that man was in some unknown place, being hunted by whoever was going to be searching for Elzaiya, giving Elzaiya free rein to work. But that was just the first part of the plan.
"What we need is to make sure that, somehow, whatever we do works. If not, it's all for nothing," Alpheus concluded.
"Are you sure everything will be okay?" Hadeezah reached out for Elzaiya's hand.

"There is no perfect plan." He took her hand and pulled her close to him. He took in her scent. She smelt just right. 'Lovely' was cliché. She was the scent of nectar at 6:30 am in a meadow opening up to the warm rays of the morning sun. The scent of brown that made coffee so lovable. She was feminine and smelt like a woman... like his wife. She smelt like the person who woke up on the other side of his bed.
"What's making you smile like that now? It's so creepy," she whispered. "You're having perverse thoughts, aren't you?"
"Considering that he nearly slept with his late sister, and then there's Helen, 'perverse' isn't far from the things he's capable of," Merceides said.
"But he told me he apologised for what he did then." Hadeezah turned a sympathetic face towards Merceides. "Are you still holding a grudge?"
"No... I... No... Of course not. I—"
"I'm just messing with you, Merci," she giggled. "It's so adorable how you fall for it every time."
"You..." Merceides clenched his fist and stood up.
"I'm out!" He declared and then pointed at them both. "You two deserve each other. But thank God your kids have good people as their uncles."
The others laughed as he made his way out.

Alpheus also stood up and declared his intention to leave. “I'll keep you updated and will keep a low profile from hereon. I hope this plan works. Cos, in my opinion, it really stretches a bit too far.
“Don't worry about it, Al,” Machiavelli consoled him. “I've been with Elzaiya the longest. I'm still alive, aren't I?”
“Usually by the skin of your teeth,” Merceides said. “Still, he does come up with plans that work. Crazy plans, but they work. Let's trust him this time, too.”

“Thanks a lot, you all," Elzaiya spoke. "I really appreciate you putting your trust in me. I know it hasn't been easy, especially on you, Merceides. Harlequin’s our brother… and even though, Mother… it's okay if—”
“We have to keep the next generation safe, brother,” Merceides said. “That's your responsibility. I trust you'll do it better than I can.”
“Thank you. That means a lot to me,” Elzaiya nodded.
“We'll be seeing each other soon,” Merceides said and stepped out.
“Let's go and leave the lovers to their thing,” Cairo said.
The others waved and said their goodbyes before leaving.
Finally, the house was silent, and it was Elzaiya and Hadeezah alone in the living room.
“You didn't tell them everything,” she said.
“It's part of the plan. Telling them will change the way it all plays out.
“But it might keep some of them safe. I'm just concerned that you might needlessly be putting them in danger without them even knowing why.”
“I wish it were optimal. I would have shared it all with them. But the truth is, each person knows as much as they need to know.”
“And how much do I know, El? Only what I need to know?”
“Deezah, no. Don't do that with me.”
“Then share these things with me.”
“I won't, Deezah. I can, but I won't.”
“Why? What is love if we can't—”
“This doesn't change the nature of our love, Deezah.”
“Just the colour of its flame? And stop calling my name in every sentence…”
She snuggled into his arms and held him. “Why won't you share them with me and make your burden lighter?”
“It’s because I love you that I want to carry this one alone. I don't want you to bear the burden of having to lie to those you love.”
“If you put it like that, it's—”
“I want you to remain innocently beautiful.”

He had watched the house for two weeks now and was sure that this was the right safehouse. The men who went in and out of the house pretended to be tenants living in the apartment, but people with authority had airs about them, and anyone trained to serve the government had an air about them that reeked especially of entitlement. They thought themselves better than the civilians they swore to protect, and that was how he found them.

The hideout was a two-bedroom apartment on the third floor of the building where the men came in and out pretending to be poker buddies or something. The man in witness protection, however, rarely came out. He looked at the man's picture again, to be sure. He was the same man he'd seen come out twice from the house and who hadn't gone past the lawn. He shoved the picture in his pocket and picked up his gun. It was cocked and ready. He put on his gloves and wrapped his fingers around the weapon, then drew a deep breath.
“I hope they're bad shots,” he said aloud and chuckled to himself.
He found it comical that someone like him would be shot. He'd been doing this for too long to get caught now or die, even.
He left the engine running and walked into the building.

When he got to the third floor of the building, he scanned the area for the noisiest place. It was all camouflage, using noise to cover up for one of them being less frequently seen. Normal people won't even take note.
He paused for a moment, then reached for his jacket and touched the canister hidden inside. He changed his mind and went forward. There was no need for such drastic measures.
He'd studied the apartment for weeks. He knew where he was going and how to go about this job.

He knocked and took two steps back, then waited for footsteps to approach. Before the man at the door could pause and draw his gun before opening the door, for precaution’s sake, he slammed his foot into the door, crashing it on the man inside, and then, bending down, took three quick shots.

His last bullet caught the victim square in the chest. Seeing that his task was done, he brought out the canister, threw it into the room, and shot at it. He closed his eyes and dived towards the stairs, got into the car and sped away. The unwelcome embrace of teargas racing after him.
Some minutes later, he called his contact and said those two prideful words every employer loved to hear: “It's done.”
There was no reply, just a vibration as the rest of his payment entered his account.
“Nice doing business with you, motherfucker!” He said into the line that had long gone dead.
Elzaiya stared at the scene of the crime that was displayed on the news and sighed. Hadeezah held his hand and shut her eyes.
“I shudder to think you could have been the one,” she muttered. She sank her head onto his lap and lay there, her eyes closed.
“To think people you once knew will want to do that to you. It's so cruel.”
“Alpheus said they were prepared for an assault, but I'm sure they didn't expect someone so skilled,” Elzaiya replied.

“I'm afraid, El,” she said, curling up in the chair. “What if they don't believe the plan? You said your father… You said Emerson is smart, and so is Harlequin. Then there's your mother. They're just as formidable as you, Machiavelli, Alpheus, Merceides, and Kane. What if—”
“Shhhh…” Elzaiya put his hands to his lips. “Can you hear that?”
“What?” She raised herself to meet his wandering gaze, and his lips fell on hers instead.
“The sound of you being afraid,” he said.
She wanted to hiss, but he was holding her behind the neck. He kissed her again and ran his fingers through her hair.
“You don't have to worry about anything, Deezah,” he said. “Trust me. I have it all planned out. This time, it'll all end well. Everything will be resolved.”
She was about to reply when the news reporter went on:

“And so far, there hasn't been a sighting of the assailant, and his whereabouts remain unknown. However, as fortune would have it, of the two witnesses who happened to be present in the safe house that day, only one of them was killed. Now that one of the witnesses is dead, it has been revealed that the safe house that was attacked was, in fact, a double safe house, one tasked with the protection of another witness for an entirely different case.

“As it turns out, the dead witness happens to be Evander, the heir and only son of Aleks Evander, the Billionaire of the East, founder of Evander Oils, among so many other enterprises. The question now on everyone's minds is, “What does the future hold for Emerson and his accomplices now that they've crossed the line of a man with the capacity to drag them out into the light?”
“Was this all part of your plan?” Hadeezah asked. Her face was flushed, partly from admiration and partly from shock.
“I can't confirm or deny it. But it is obvious that it works well in our favour,” Elzaiya replied.
“El…”

He kissed her again. “Deezah… we may not have much time left together. I don't want to spend the little that we might have talking about things that don't matter. What's important is that you're here right now, as am I. I love you, Hadeezah. Everything else is a manifestation of what I would do to keep you safe. I don't want to be judged for loving you in all the ways I can. I only want to love and be loved by you. I am a man who barely asks much from others. The little I require, I so desire that they be granted unto me.”
“You're so…”
She moaned as his warm hand rested on her thigh.
“So…”
She giggled. “So what, husband? Let me love you. You're all that matters.”
Kane watched the man closely and felt abhorrence creep through him. At first, he'd wanted to decline the offer Elzaiya had presented, but he'd seen reason and, for that reason, had accepted.

Elzaiya had not tried to buy him over with some noble ideal like most people would. Grand ideals of making the world a better place by getting rid of scum like this killer. No. He'd simply told him the truth and had asked him for his help.

“My father… not Quinn. My biological father, Emerson, killed the first person I ever fell in love with. I forgave him. Now, he's turned my brother against the family and has taken my mother fully to his side. He stole my father's wife and broke a happy marriage, a happy home. My father, Quinn, forgave him. He was willing to let his wife make her choice. But that was not enough. My mother killed him for Emerson.

"Kane, Emerson kills all that he comes across. This is no mere act of revenge nor some righteously idealistic thing that must be done. This is simply me, killing the father I don't know so that the love I have… what I know, will be safe. So that I can move into the future with a blank slate, without fear that a ghost will come haunting me from the past.

"Truth is, I've grown to love the things that I have now and the peace of mind that comes with them. Harlequin, my mother, and Emerson were always the ones who brought in chaos to the kindness that my father, Quinn, represented. I want to keep everyone safe, especially Hadeezah. I don't care if I have to kill my mother, my father, and my brother to do so. But I'll keep her safe, whatever it takes.”
The determination of a man who would do what was required for whatever reasons that were most justifiable to him. That, he could understand and respect. After all, he was no different.
He watched the man dance with some girls and waited. He wanted to do it in the water where everyone was swimming.
He'd observed the man's routine. He usually swam around this time, so he had made it his routine to go into the water before the man did to avoid looking suspicious.
Kane put on his diving mask and jumped into the water from the cliff. Some girls clapped, and the man sneered. He then swam to a shallow part of the water and waited. The man usually swam there.
Kane drew out his syringe and waited. The toxin was a paralytic. Once the man was paralysed, he would drag him under and suffocate him. The best part was how he intended to do it.

Kane waited until he felt the splash. He raised his head and confirmed that it was his target. He then swam underneath to where the man splashed around and pricked his feet with the syringe. It took exactly 10 seconds for the man's movements to halt, and then, like dead weight, he sank.

Kane then removed his own diving mask, still connected to his oxygen tank, and placed it on the man's face. The man took a deep breath. Kane signalled for him to hold his breath and then pulled him underwater. The man did so, thinking Kane was there to help. How trusting for a man who'd spent his whole life killing.
Underwater, Kane pulled out the air-filled ziplock bag in his swimming trunks and placed it over the man's face, holding it tight.

The man barely struggled. About 15 minutes later, Kane disposed of the bag and raised the man's head above water, yelling for help. By the time the medical team arrived, the man was dead. He'd died underwater and apparently had not drowned but suffocated.
Killing was art. And as he left, Kane wondered if he missed doing this.
“I just saw the news. Did you really do it?”
“No! I would never. I thought it was you. That's why I was reaching out earlier,” Aaira replied. “Tell me again that it wasn't you.”
“Mom! I wouldn't dare make a move on my own without consulting you both. But now that it's done, there's the problem of the Evanders coming for us.”
“That's a pain,” Aaira sighed. “I'll get to you soon. Let me find out more.”
“Okay.” Harlequin hung up.
It was either that she was lying or Emerson was playing them both.

Harlequin knew not to trust anyone, especially not when his mother had just killed his father, when she couldn't love him any less. At this point, he'd started regretting the decisions he'd made. But they'd been made, and he'll stick with them.
“You tried to kill our son,” Aaira yelled, throwing a pillow at Emerson, whose expression remained unchanged.
“Aren't you going to defend yourself?”
“Na’ah,” was all he said.
“We'd better start figuring out what to do about the Evanders,” she said.
Emerson said nothing.
Exasperated, she hissed and left the room.
A few moments later, Emerson picked up the cocktail beside him and took a sip, then smiled. “Boy… has he grown.”

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.title: Lex Ferrea Necessitatis
paras: Aleks Evander was a man who had risen from his station by grit, violence, and murder. The justification for his actions lay in the conviction that God rewards those who, by righteousness, do only what is essential in the necessity that growth presents. Any more than that, he condemned as greed. It was hypocrisy, Elzaiya knew, but who wasn't one?
Better a man who considered himself righteous than one who killed because it was an available preference.

He smiled at the thought. Here he was comparing killer to killer when he stood somewhere on the spectrum with a vain justification for why the people he sought deserved to die. If all things went well today, he would mask his actions with the ideals of justice, not the pettiness of revenge. But that was only if all things went well. If they didn't, he'll—
“We're here, sir,” his driver said as she stopped the car.
He inhaled deeply and settled his anxiety, then proceeded to open the door.
“It will be fine, sir,” his driver said.
“Thank you, Jade.” He smiled and stepped out.
“You'll—”
“Round and back, sir,” she grinned. “I know.”
He shook his head. “Alright… alright… I'll see you around.”
“Get me souvenirs, sir, okay?” She yelled after him.
He waved his hand in response, and she drove away.

Such a troublesome girl. Jade was 19, at the top of her class in mechanical engineering. She'd graduated from school a year ago. But instead of searching for jobs like most people her age, she'd applied something she considered a more efficient strategy.

First, she'd researched the new head of the Quinn family and found that he kept a close-knit circle. These people, practically family, were well cared for and protected. These included the cook and his driver.
More research revealed that his driver had recently travelled out of the country to manage a small family business but was still being paid a stipend by the Quinn family.

Jade, seeing this as an opportunity, decided to approach Elzaiya one day as he was out shopping with Hadeezah. He usually took his wife out alone with no security at night or at odd hours when they wouldn't be spotted or disturbed.

It was 8:45 p.m. on a Thursday, and the parking lot was empty. She sat on the hood of the car and waited for them to finish shopping. When they came out, they met her sitting on Elzaiya's blue BMW RLX VII, face cap over her face, asleep.
“What do you think you're doing?” Elzaiya demanded.
She jumped up, startled. Her cap fell.
“Take it easy, El. She's just a girl,” Hadeezah said, upon seeing her face.
“I was only…” Jade started.
“Couldn't you just open the door like a normal person and lie down inside?” He asked. “What if you scratch the windscreen?”
“What?” Jade couldn't believe it. Neither could Hadeezah.
“You left the car open?” Hadeezah was beside herself. “What if—”
“Remember the girl I told you about last month? The one who was researching and stalking us?” Elzaiya casually asked while opening the doors to drop the groceries in the car.
“Yes?”
“This is she. Name's Jade. Mechanical engineering. The question is, what does Jade, the best graduating student of her class, want with us?”
“You knew!” Jade was speechless.
“Well, come on, Jade, what do you—”
“I want to work for you, sir. I want to be your personal driver.”
There was a moment of silence, and then Elzaiya burst into a chuckle. After some minutes, he restrained himself and asked the pressing question, “Why?”

“Because you take care of those around you, sir. I come from a poor family. My parents did everything short of selling organs to put me through school. I know that they have grand plans for me and want me to get a good job and become someone respectable in society. But honestly, sir, that's bullshit.

"My parents have done what they can for me. I want to honour their sacrifice by doing what I can for them. For me, that means getting a high-paying job that can take care of everyone in the family as soon as possible. The less stress involved, the better. I want to watch them sow what they've reaped in me before thinking of what's respectable and grand.

"I know you pay your workers well, and you take good care of those around you. But as your driver, I'm also an excellent mechanic and can take care of all the cars in the family. If you eventually open a company for me, we can split the profit, and you can grow your wealth by helping me grow.
For now, all I ask is that you give me a chance to—”
“Take the keys, Jade.”
Elzaiya tossed the keys to Jade and opened the door for Hadeezah, who got in. He went in beside her and shut the door.
It took a moment for Jade to collect herself. When she did, she opened the driver's door, got in, started the car, and they sped away. She's been his driver ever since.

“The famous third son,” Aleks said, stretching his hands to Elzaiya, who approached him casually and extended his hand. The man shook it and covered it with his other hand. Elzaiya was on high alert. You never knew with Russians.
“Please come in,” Aleks said. His English was a bit shaky, but good enough to flow.”
Elzaiya restrained himself from telling the man that they could speak Russian. Better to tread softly.
Inside the mansion, Elzaiya couldn't help but be impressed. The Quinns may be wealthy, but this man was ahead by 45%. For someone who was visiting, you'd think this was his real home.
Aleks led him to a seat at his desk in what appeared to be his office and immediately went down to business.
“Those bastards. They kill a man's son for wanting to say the truth.”
“I barely made it out alive,” Elzaiya said, shivering, more from his lies being found out than from the events Aleks and the world perceived as the truth.
“Here, some whisky.” Aleks handed him a glass and filled one himself. Elzaiya sipped his after the man had gulped his own and was pouring himself a refill.
“It can be jittery, you know… gunpoint. But real men know death is always knocking.”
Whether real men accept it when it takes others is what we're here to find out. Elzaiya thought.
“After all that happened, I knew I wouldn't be safe under government protection. It's why I returned.”

“The government couldn't keep their power safe if someone wanted to steal it from them. It's why politicians should be in our pockets. We control what happens. But my son didn't listen. He said it was the right thing to do. He said if a man like you could do it, then he could too. He had information on several crimes committed by Emerson, in addition to the others. These crimes, you see, caused problems for our business in the oil regions.”
“I understand. He told me about it.” Elzaiya sipped his drink. “Not what he wanted to confess to, but the nature of the crimes. We bonded there.”
“I'm glad he met you.” Aleks put his hand on Elzaiya's shoulder. “You were one of the last people to see him alive. Tell me, did he die a good death?”
“He did. He protected me, too, and shot back, but the killer was skilled. Still, he felt no pain. He died smiling and said to make sure justice prevails.”
“My son!” Aleks raised his glass.
It was a good thing the man was too busy to know his son. But death changes people. Elzaiya raised his glass too, toasted to Evander, and took a sip.
“It was in pursuit of justice for both our wrongs, and for my friend's sake, that I hunted down the killer and took his life,” Elzaiya said.
“You found Evander’s killer?” Aleks was more overjoyed than he could hide.
“Before he died, Evander gave me a description of the killer's tattoo. After I escaped, I was able to find the killer, and I took care of it. Evander can rest in peace now.”
“Good!” Aleks slapped his palm onto the table. “That is what a man should do.”
“Yes,” he took another sip.
“But you know, there is more to be done,” Aleks said cautiously as if trying not to spoil the rapport they were building.
“You mean to speak of Emerson, Aaira, and Harlequin?”
“Yes. They are responsible for the tragedy that befell my son. And you… It is you they sought to kill. Are you not enraged?”
“It is because of it that I've come.” Elzaiya trembled a bit and let it show.
Aleks reached out and steadied his hands. “Here. More whisky.”
“Thanks.” Elzaiya swallowed it all and felt the burn, then dropped the glass slowly on the table.
“I want to find them before they find us,” he said. “Because if—”
The scent of perfume interrupted him, and he turned to face the direction it floated from. His eyes settled on the figure of a lady standing by the door, looking directly at him.

The woman was a thing of understated allure. Her fair skin was flawless, and in the light of the sun, it glowed as if she emanated a soft, warm yellow. Her eyes were hazel brown, and her thick lashes were just the perfect style.

She had high cheekbones that gave her face an elegant contour, and her lips were full with a dull shade of oxblood that did not scream desperation. When their eyes met, she softly parted her lips and smiled at him. He could tell from afar that those lips were made for secrets.
Her chestnut hair cascaded in glossy waves, and a small pearl comb was tucked into one side, holding her locks back just enough to reveal the graceful curve of her neck.

She wore a white lace dress that made her look angelic, but the way the fabric clung to her was purely devilish. The neckline of the gown dipped modestly but tantalisingly enough to hint at her hidden beauty.
She stared at Elzaiya for a moment before approaching them at the table. Elzaiya stood up as she came.
“I've seen you before,” she said, straining to recollect. “You're—”
“Elzaiya.”
“The third son!” She recalled.
“Yes, I am. And you are Irina. Evander told me about you.”
“Did he?” She said.
“Nothing much and nothing good,” Elzaiya said. “I think he lied.”
She chuckled. “I like you.” She tapped his arm and greeted her father.
“Good morning, Papa.”
“Dobroye utro, Irina.” He replied.

Elzaiya observed that, unlike most families at this level of wealth, where the father and the daughter were estranged, she seemed reasonably free with her father and a bit too jovial for someone whose brother had just died.”
“I am saddened by my brother's demise,” she said. “But I've mourned him. Life goes on.”
“No love lost between you two,” Elzaiya mused. “I understand.”

“You were telling Father that you want to find Emerson and the rest of your family before they come for you. You are like a Russian that way. I'd always thought you'd be softer. You know, since you're… not.”
Elzaiya smiled. “For better or worse, I am Emerson's son.”
There was silence for a moment, and then she laughed nervously. “I would like to help you,” she said.
His threat had not gone unnoticed.
She walked to the sofa on the other side of the office and sat down. Elzaiya, too, took his seat and resumed his request.
“With Emerson free, I can't live peacefully,” Elzaiya said. “I need this to be resolved. That's why I came to you. You have more reach than I do.”
“As Irina has said, we'll help you,” Aleks said.
“Thank you.”
“But, under one condition,” Aleks added.
“What's that?”
“They all die. Not just Emerson. Your brother and your mother, too. When we do this, we want the circle to end once and for all. There will be no end if any of them are left alive.”
Elzaiya shook his head. “I thought you might say so, and I've already considered it an option. I agree. They all die.”
Then it's settled.
They both shook hands, and Elzaiya stood up to leave, but then Irina stood up and called him back.
“Your Abuja has beautiful places. We visited, and you wouldn't even give a girl a tour?”
Elzaiya smiled. “Okay? Let's take a tour of the city then.”
She walked over to where he stood and slung her hand into his. “See ya, Papa.”
Aleks Evander waved them away, and they walked out. Jade was already waiting in front of the house with the car doors open. They both slid inside, and the doors shut automatically.
“Neat,” Irina said. “I see you have great taste in cars and in women.”
“You are speaking of my wife?”
“And your driver, and me?” She said that and then rested her hand on his thigh. He let it lie there.
“So, from what part of your story did you start bullshitting my father?”
“I don't understand what you mean?” He appeared perplexed.
Jade stole a peek at him from the rearview mirror. He ignored her.
Irina laughed and let it slide. “Okay, smart.”
“Where to, sir?” Jade asked.
“Somewhere where there's water and a place to eat,” Elzaiya said.
“Got it!”
“I've got the sense, Elzaiya, that all your women want to sleep with you,” Irina teased.
“Yet, I've only got eyes for my wife,” he replied. “What does the rest matter?”
“She must be a stunner to make a woman like me, who's among the rest, not matter.”
“She is. But beyond that exists my choice. I have loved her once as a different man when she bore a different name. I want to love her better now in all the ways that I can.”
“Men like you are rare,” Irina whispered, her lips almost touching his ear, her hand inching up his thigh. “You keep making yourself irresistible.”

Elzaiya smiled, then, placing his hand on her thigh in turn, faced her and whispered something back into her ear. She looked down and then laughed and faced forward, silent through the rest of the ride.
They went to the beach and then to some resorts, and Irina indulged herself in several Nigerian dishes. She was quite taken by them.
Jade sat with them and observed Elzaiya’s composure through all of her flirting.
When they were done, Jade drove them back to the house that Aleks Evander was renting for the duration of their stay and dropped Irina off.
“Today was a very lovely day,” she said when she alighted. “Let's do it again sometime.”
“Sure,” Elzaiya said and waved as Jade drove away.
“She was totally into you,” Jade burst into laughter as they drove out of the residence.
“Right?” Elzaiya said. “She is something.”
“You know, sir, I wonder how you do it,” Jade commented. “I know it wouldn't be easy if it were me. All these women…”
“I’ve adapted,” he said simply. “It's easier dealing with each problem as it comes than having a modus operandi for specific types of problems.”
“You just referred to women as problems. Ain't that a tad sexist, sir?”
“Yes, it is. Your point being?”
She sighed. “For a wealthy man who's so brilliant, you couldn't care less about opinion, could you?”
“Not when it doesn't make sense.” He raised a finger. “Jade, remember this—”
“Only knowledgeable and well-informed opinions matter,” she completed.
He grinned. “You've learnt something.”
“So, are we going home?” They were at the south gate of the Quinn residence.
“Not yet. Take me to Helen's.”
“Will you need anything, sir? Drinks, cigars, coffee, aphrodisiacs, condoms?”
“You walk around with condoms? You sure suffered a foul upbringing,” Elzaiya teased her back.
They both laughed together.
“Please be careful, sir. Hadeezah loves you. Helen wants you… You know how these things go.”
“I'll be careful. Thanks, Jade.”
“Sure thing.” They arrived, and she stopped the car in front of Helen's apartment. “I'll be waiting.”
“I won't take long.”

Elzaiya alighted from the vehicle and knocked on the door. After a moment, Helen opened the door. Motherhood had not changed her, and even though they met often, she looked more beautiful each time. It was like she intentionally set out to compete with Hadeezah for his affection.
She stood effortlessly in front of him; her hair was dyed chestnut brown and was braided in long strands that fell onto her shoulders with strays across her face. Elzaiya brushed them away.
“It's been a while; I was beginning to think you hated me,” she said.

Her features were accentuated by almond-shaped hazel eyes that seemed to hold a hypnotic gleam. A faint, almost imperceptible scar curved along her arm where she'd injured herself some time ago while moving furniture. She'd called him late that night…
She wore a green and brown flowery top that clung perfectly to her lithe figure and extended down past her waist to somewhere above her knees, complementing her slender legs in the dim light.
“I don't hate you. Mostly just avoiding you.” He smiled at her, and she reached out her arm and tugged at his shirt.
“El… I…”
He placed his hand on the back of her head and pulled her close.
“I can't do that to Hadeezah,” was all he said.
“I know you won't. I just wish you'd consider the fact that you can have more than one woman in your life.”
He laughed.
“Will you come see Alasdair?” She stared up at him.
“Sure.”
She went in, and he followed her, shutting the door behind him. Inside, he followed her to the room where Alasdair sat, his toys sprawled all around him.
The boy’s eyes lit up when he saw Elzaiya.
“Da Da,” he called.
“Hey there, brother,” Elzaiya called back.
He approached where the boy sat and cleared some toys away, then sat down and crossed his legs.

The boy had undeniable traits, even at just a year old. His fluffy, jet-black curls framed a cherubic face that held innocent blue-green eyes that contrasted with the warm undertone of his skin, which mirrored his mother's hazel complexion.

His tiny nose had a delicate, straight bridge like Elzaiya's, and his lips curled naturally into a mischievous smile, a signature trait they'd both gotten from Emerson. A faint dimple appeared on his right cheek whenever he giggled, softening the sharp edges of his lineage.
He picked up one of his toys and handed it to Elzaiya, who reached out and then withdrew his hand just as the boy did the same thing.

They both giggled and did it again, then Elzaiya made snarling noises and roared at him. The boy roared back, and they fumed at each other for some time before the boy finally relinquished one of his toys. Elzaiya accepted it humbly and thanked him, then promised to get him a new one.
The boy nodded and smiled at him, then waved as he stood up.
“Ba-Bye,” Alastair said.
Elzaiya chuckled. “Bye, baby brother.”
Helen watched them both and walked Elzaiya to the living room, smiling.
“I'm always relieved when you come to see him. Alastair never gets along with other children, just you, Kane, and Machiavelli, but mostly you.”
Her eyes searched his face. “Please stay the night, El. Please?”

“Helen…” he sighed. “He bent and kissed her full on the lips. She inhaled deeply and wrapped her arms around his lower back. He stepped into the disappearing space between them and pushed her back, pushing his body into hers. His hand slid down her back to her waist and down to her supple behind, and then, slowly, he disengaged. She reluctantly let him.

“You have my father's son,” he said. “We can't have what you want, the way you want it. And even though Hadeezah is fine with you being the only other woman I can have in my life this way, it will complicate things for Alastair. I want my brother to have a happy childhood. A normal one as much as possible. We don't know what can affect his psyche. I want him to do better than Emerson and me.”
She said nothing and stared at him as he walked away to the car.
“Goodnight,” she finally said when he was about to get in.
“See you soon,” he replied.

She smiled and watched them drive away. Alastair had developed a very troubling pattern, but it was one that she'd come to like. Whenever he gave Elzaiya one of his toys, he expected his brother back within a week with a new one. After Alastair’s first bout, Elzaiya always returned.
She knew she would see him soon.
